extracted.intended_audience: readers and students of political philosophy; scholars and general readers of Hobbes' Leviathan
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of Hobbes's enumerated 'Laws of Nature' and related principles about persons, authority, and commonwealth from Leviathan; these are normative rules for conduct, judgement, and political organization in Hobbes's account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nothing Done To A Man, By His Own Consent Can Be Injury
rubrics_metrics.description: Whatsoever is done to a man, conformable to his own Will signified to the doer, is no Injury to him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the doer has not passed away his original right by antecedent covenant, there is no breach of covenant and therefore no injury; if the will is a release of covenant, again no injury.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justice Commutative, And Distributive
rubrics_metrics.description: Justice of actions is divided intocommutative (equality of value in contracts) and distributive (distribution of equal benefit to those of equal merit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commutative justice = justice of a contractor (performance of covenant in buying/selling, hiring, lending, exchanging). Distributive justice is more properly 'equity' or the act of an arbitrator defining what is just. Merit outside covenant is not owed by justice but rewarded by grace; value contracted for is measured by the appetite of the contractors (the just value is what they consent to give).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fourth Law Of Nature — Gratitude
rubrics_metrics.description: That a man which receiveth Benefit from another of meer Grace, endeavour that he which giveth it, have no reasonable cause to repent him of his good will.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gratitude (observing antecedent grace) is necessary to maintain benevolence, trust, mutual help, and reconciliation; breach is ingratitude, analogous to injustice with respect to covenant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fifth Law Of Nature — Mutual Accommodation (Compleasance)
rubrics_metrics.description: That every man strive to accommodate himselfe to the rest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because human aptness for society varies, those who refuse to adapt (retain superfluities others need or are stubborn in passions) obstruct social building and may be cast out; observers of this law are 'sociable' (commodi), violators are stubborn, insociable, froward, intractable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sixth Law Of Nature — Facility To Pardon
rubrics_metrics.description: That upon caution of the Future time, a man ought to pardon the offences past of them that repenting, desire it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pardon is granting of peace; refusing to pardon those who give security of future good is an aversion to peace and contrary to the law of nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seventh Law Of Nature — In Revenges Respect Only The Future Good
rubrics_metrics.description: That in Revenges (retribution of evil for evil) Men look not at the greatnesse of the evill past, but the greatnesse of the good to follow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Punishment must be inflicted only for correction of the offender or as example for others; revenge merely to triumph or glory in another's hurt is vain-glory, contrary to reason, and tends to war (cruelty).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eighth Law Of Nature — Against Contumely
rubrics_metrics.description: That no man by deed, word, countenance, or gesture, declare Hatred, or Contempt of another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signs of hatred or contempt provoke fighting because many would rather hazard life than not be revenged; breach of this law is called contumely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ninth Law Of Nature — Against Pride
rubrics_metrics.description: That every man acknowledge other for his Equall by Nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because natural equality is the proper starting point and inequality is introduced by civil laws, failure to acknowledge equality (pride) undermines peace; admission of equality is necessary for entering conditions of peace on equal terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tenth Law Of Nature — Against Arrogance
rubrics_metrics.description: That at the entrance into conditions of Peace, no man require to reserve to himselfe any Right, which he is not content should be reserved to every one of the rest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When making peace men must lay down certain rights; one must not demand special reservations for oneself that one would deny others (pleonexia — desire of more than one's share). Observers are modest, breakers are arrogant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eleventh Law Of Nature — Equity
rubrics_metrics.description: If a man be trusted to judge between man and man, it is a precept of the Law of Nature, that he deale Equally between them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partiality in judgment deters use of judges and arbitrators and leads to war; observance (equal distribution to each what in reason belongs to him) is equity; violation is acception of persons (prosopolepsia).

rubrics_metrics.name: Twelfth Law Of Nature — Equal Use Of Things Common
rubrics_metrics.description: That such things as cannot be divided, be enjoyed in Common, if it can be; and if the quantity of the thing permit, without Stint; otherwise Proportionably to the number of them that have Right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If common enjoyment isn't possible without diminution, allocate proportionally to rights-holders to preserve equity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thirteenth Law Of Nature — Of Lot
rubrics_metrics.description: That the Entire Right; or else, (making the use alternate,) the First Possession, be determined by Lot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where things cannot be divided or enjoyed in common, lot (chance) is prescribed by the law of nature as a means to achieve equal distribution; first possession or alternation may be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fourteenth Law Of Nature — Of Primogeniture And First Seising
rubrics_metrics.description: Of Lots there be two sorts, Arbitrary, and Naturall. Naturall is either Primogeniture (kleronomia) or First Seisure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Things that cannot be enjoyed in common or divided ought to be adjudged to the first possessor and in some cases to the first-born as acquired by lot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fifteenth Law Of Nature — Of Mediators
rubrics_metrics.description: It is also a Law of Nature, That all men that mediate Peace, be allowed safe Conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intercession (mediation) is a means commanded by the law that seeks peace; mediators must be protected by safe conduct so they can perform that function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sixteenth Law Of Nature — Of Submission To Arbitrement
rubrics_metrics.description: That they that are at controversie, submit their Right to the judgement of an Arbitrator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To avoid leaving questions to force (war), parties must covenant mutually to stand to the sentence of another (an arbitrator) over questions of fact or right.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seventeenth Law Of Nature — No Man Is His Own Judge
rubrics_metrics.description: No man is a fit Arbitrator in his own cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because every man is presumed to act for his own benefit, even if fit, allowing one party to judge would deny equal admission of the other and leave the controversy unresolved (cause of war).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eighteenth Law Of Nature — No Man To Be Judge Who Has Cause Of Partiality
rubrics_metrics.description: No man in any Cause ought to be received for Arbitrator, to whom greater profit, honour, or pleasure apparently ariseth out of the victory of one party, than of the other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such a person effectively takes a bribe (even if unavoidable) and no one can be obliged to trust him; admitting such biased judges perpetuates controversy and war.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nineteenth Law Of Nature — Of Witness
rubrics_metrics.description: In a controversie of Fact, the Judge must give credit to a third (or more) as witnesses if there are no other arguments, else the question is undecided and left to force.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If one party cannot be preferred on arguments alone, the testimony of impartial witnesses is required to prevent recourse to force.

rubrics_metrics.name: A Rule For Examining The Laws Of Nature — The Golden Rule
rubrics_metrics.description: "Do not that to another, which thou wouldest not have done to thy selfe."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh the actions of others with your own; if they seem too heavy to put on the other's side of the balance (while your own passions/self-love add nothing), the law points that the Laws of Nature are reasonable and must be observed as guiding conduct toward peace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation Of The Laws Of Nature — In Foro Interno vs Externo
rubrics_metrics.description: The Laws of Nature oblige in conscience (in foro interno) always; but in effect (in foro externo — putting them in act) only when there is security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A person who obeys laws of nature where no one else does makes himself prey; thus external obligation is conditional on security. Actions that technically conform to the law may still break its obligation if the agent believes they are contrary; laws binding only as a desire/endeavour means fulfilment requires unfeigned and constant endeavour, not impossible sacrifice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immutable And Practical Character Of The Laws Of Nature
rubrics_metrics.description: The Laws of Nature are immutable and eternal; vices like injustice, ingratitude, arrogance can never be made lawful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although eternal, the laws are 'easy' because they oblige only to a desire and endeavour; to endeavour their performance is to fulfil them and to be just.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Science Of These Laws — True Moral Philosophy
rubrics_metrics.description: The science of the Laws of Nature is the true and only moral philosophy: the study of what conduceth to the conservation and defence of men in society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moral virtues and vices are properly understood as means to peaceable, sociable, and comfortable living rather than mere mediocrity of passions; this is how virtues should be judged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition Of A Person
rubrics_metrics.description: A PERSON is he 'whose words or actions are considered, either as his own, or as representing the words or actions of an other man, or of any other thing to whom they are attributed, whether Truly or by Fiction.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personhood covers natural persons (considered as their own) and feigned/artificial persons (representatives whose words/actions stand for another).

rubrics_metrics.name: Person Natural And Artificial
rubrics_metrics.description: When words/actions are considered as his own he is a Naturall Person; when considered as representing another, he is a Feigned or Artificial Person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Term 'person' derives from stage persona; personating is acting or representing oneself or another (representative, lieutenant, vicar, attorney, deputy, procurator, actor).

rubrics_metrics.name: Actor, Author, Authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Of artificial persons some have their words and actions owned by those whom they represent: the Actor acts; he that owneth his words and actions is the AUTHOR; that right of doing any act is called AUTHORITY.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authority is always a right to do an act; what is done 'by authority' is done by commission or licence from him whose right it is.

rubrics_metrics.name: Covenants By Authority Bind The Author (Not Necessarily The Actor)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Actor maketh a Covenant by Authority, he bindeth thereby the Author, no lesse than if he had made it himselfe; but only so far as is within the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All the nature of covenants between men in their natural capacity holds where made by their actors or representatives so far as authorized; contracting with an actor without knowing his authority is at the covenantor's peril.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liability When Actor Acts Against Law By Command
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Actor doth any thing against the Law of Nature by command of the Author, if he be obliged by former Covenant to obey him, the Author, not the Actor, breaketh the Law of Nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refusal by the actor to do it (when bound to obey) would itself be contrary to the Law of Nature forbidding breach of covenant; responsibility lies with the author who commanded the illicit act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority Must Be Shown For Covenants Made By Mediation
rubrics_metrics.description: If the covenant-maker mediated by an actor and the authority is not made manifest upon demand, the covenant is no longer obligatory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A covenant made with the author via an actor is invalid without counter-assurance; but if one expected only the actor's word, the actor may be treated as the author and the covenant stands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Things Inanimate May Be Personated But Cannot Be Authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Inanimate things (church, hospital, bridge) may be personated by a rector, master, or overseer, but inanimate things cannot be Authors and therefore cannot give authority to their actors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actors may have authority given by owners/governors; such personation requires some state of civil government and cannot occur before introduction of civil government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Irrational Persons May Be Personated By Guardians
rubrics_metrics.description: Children, fools, and mad-men who have no use of reason may be personated by guardians or curators; they can be no authors during that time, but may later own actions when they recover reason.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During the period of non-reason, the right of governing them may give authority to guardians; this concept presumes civil state since before that there is no dominion of persons.

rubrics_metrics.name: False Gods May Be Personated But Cannot Be Authors
rubrics_metrics.description: An idol or mere figment may be personated (as gods of the heathen) and held possessions and rights dedicated to them, but idols cannot be authors because an idol is nothing; authority proceeds from the state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before civil government, the gods of heathens could not be personated; the state's appointment provided the authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: The True God May Be Personated
rubrics_metrics.description: The true God may be personated: e.g., Moses governed the Israelites in God's name, Jesus was sent by his Father, the Holy Ghost spoke and worked in the apostles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Representation in God's name differs from acting in one's own name; this is historical justification of certain forms of religious personation.

rubrics_metrics.name: A Multitude Made One Person By Representation
rubrics_metrics.description: A Multitude of men are made One Person when they are by one man, or one Person, represented with the consent of every one of that Multitude in particular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unity of the representer, not unity of the represented, makes the person one; the representer bears the person and is the one person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Every One Is Author (In The Representative Union)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each member of the multitude gives authority from himself to their common representer in particular and owns all the actions the representer doth when authority is given without stint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If commission is limited, none of them owns more than they gave; the multitude is not one by nature but many authors making the representative their author.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actor May Be Many Men Made One By Plurality Of Voices
rubrics_metrics.description: If the representative consist of many men, the voice of the greater number must be considered as the voice of them all.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When votes are divided, the excess of negatives standing uncontradicted are the only voice the representative has; plurality determines the representative's voice as long as it was consented to by each.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representatives When Number Is Even May Be Unprofitable
rubrics_metrics.description: A representative of even number, especially when the number is not great, is often mute and incapable of action because contradictory voices are oftentimes equal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In certain cases equality of votes can determine (e.g., not condemning is absolving), but overall parity may render an assembly unable to act; deadlock is unfit for governance especially in war.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negative Voice (Veto) And Dangers Of Small Multiplied Representatives
rubrics_metrics.description: In odd-numbered bodies where each member has a negative voice to take away the effect of all affirmative voices, the assembly may become a mute person unapt for government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diversity of opinions and interests in small representative numbers can make them unable to act in cases of great consequence, making them unfit for governing a multitude, especially in time of war.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two Sorts Of Authors — Simple Authors And Conditional Authors (Sureties)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors simply called are those who own the action of another simply; second kind own an action conditionally — undertaking to do it if the other does not by a certain time (suretyes, fidejussores, sponsore; praedes for debt; vades for appearance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These conditional authorship forms (sureties) specify different liabilities and roles in obligations and acts; they are relevant in contractual and judicial processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generation And Definition Of A Common-wealth
rubrics_metrics.description: The only way to erect a Common Power able to defend men and secure them from invasion and mutual injury is to confer all their power and strength upon one man or one assembly, reducing many wills into one will — making one person whose acts the multitude own.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is achieved by mutual covenant 'every man with every man' authorising and giving up the right of governing oneself to the sovereign (one person), who thereby has the use of the collective power to form wills to peace and common defence; distinguishes commonwealth by institution vs by acquisition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition Of A Common-wealth; Sovereign And Subject
rubrics_metrics.description: A Common-wealth (civitas) is one Person, of whose Acts a great Multitude, by mutuall Covenants one with another, have made themselves every one the Author, to the end he may use the strength and means of them all for their Peace and Common Defence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: He that beareth this Person is called SOVEREIGNE and everyone else a SUBJECT; attaining sovereign power can be by institution (mutual covenant) or by acquisition (force).
